content: The Banting Lectures are an annual series of research presentations delivered by a distinguished expert in the field of diabetes. The series is named after Frederick Banting, a pioneering scientist, physician, and Nobel laureate who co-discovered insulin. These lectures are currently organized and hosted by the American Diabetes Association. In 2006, Robert Rizza presented a lecture titled Cure, Optimal Care and Total Commitment: What if they happened tomorrow? Also in 2006, Richard Bergman delivered a lecture titled Harmony and Discord in the Orchestration of Glucose Metabolism. In 2005, Jeffrey S. Flier gave a lecture titled Critical conversations: fat, brain, and the regulation of energy balance. In 2004, Michael Brownlee presented on The pathobiology of diabetic complications: A unifying mechanism. In 2003, Aldo A. Rossini discussed Autoimmune diabetes and the circle of tolerance. In 2001, John D. McGarry delivered a lecture on Dysregulation of fatty acid metabolism in the etiology of type 2 diabetes. In 1997, Philip E. Cryer presented on Control of glucose uptake and release by the liver in vivo: Hypoglycemia as the limiting factor in the management of insulin-dependent diabetes mellitus (IDDM). In 1989, Ora M. Rosen gave a lecture titled Structure and function of insulin receptors. In 1988, Gerald M. Reaven discussed the Role of insulin resistance in human disease.
